## Abstract

The Earth's climate system exhibits complex spatiotemporal variability, making it challenging to identify large-scale patterns such as teleconnections. Studying these patterns is essential because they link large-scale climate drivers to regional impacts. In particular, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), as a well-known example, influences temperature and precipitation variability, with significant consequences for agriculture, water resources, and public health. Rather than focusing on point-wise prediction, this work aims to capture structured and recurrent patterns that characterize regional climate variability. We propose a data-driven framework for identifying climate regimes using self-supervised representation learning, employing Masked Siamese Networks (MSN) with a Vision Transformer backbone to learn latent representations of daily temperature fields over the Brazilian Cerrado. These representations are discretized into a finite set of climate states, capturing dominant spatial configurations without requiring labeled data. The resulting regimes provide a compact and interpretable representation of climate variability, enabling the analysis of their temporal organization and relationship with large-scale drivers such as ENSO. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Green-AI-Lab-GAIA/climate-clustering-forENSO-teleconnections.
